title: Commercial Space Federation (CSF) Welcomes Two New Associate Members
summary: The Commercial Space Federation (CSF) announced the addition of two new associate members, Outlier and Rendezvous Robotics, which specialize in reusable satellite platforms and adaptable technologies. This move expands the CSF's network in the commercial space sector.

title: Speed to Field Starts Below the Prime
summary: The article discusses the defense industrial base from various perspectives, including a warfighter's viewpoint and leadership in a company. It emphasizes the importance of rapid deployment in the defense sector.

title: The electronics ‘under the hood’ of space networking
summary: SpaceNews interviews Jeff Janicik, founder and chairman of Innoflight, about space networking electronics, Golden Dome, Artemis, and collaborations with the Space Development Agency.

title: LatConnect 60 and Phi Earth Partner to Connect Space and Soil
summary: LatConnect 60 and Phi Earth have partnered to integrate satellite and ground-based environmental data for nature-based projects. The collaboration aims to bridge the gap between orbital observations and field measurements.

title: RTX’s Blue Canyon Technologies introduces new spacecraft mission enabler
summary: Blue Canyon Technologies, a subsidiary of RTX, has introduced a new spacecraft subsystem designed to enhance mission capabilities for small satellites. This innovation aims to support the growing demands of the space industry.

title: The threat environment and processing at the edge
summary: FrontGrade CTO Lorne Graves discusses how spacecraft processing power is adapting to megaconstellations and the benefits of satellite edge processing with SpaceNews’ Mike Gruss.

title: Propulsion is having a moment
summary: Space propulsion technology is gaining significant attention in the space industry, as highlighted at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference. Kevin Lausten, CEO of Morpheus Space, discusses the critical role of propulsion in this trend.

title: Space Angel secures $1.75m WA Government backing to advance Western Australian spaceport plans
summary: Space Angel received a $1.75 million grant from the Western Australian Government to advance plans for a spaceport. The funding was announced by Science and Innovation Minister Stephen Dawson.

title: Tendeg Launches NewTEN Steerable Compact Antenna at SmallSat
summary: Tendeg has unveiled NewTEN, a two-axis steerable reflector antenna designed to enhance communications performance and pointing access for small spacecraft. The product was introduced at the SmallSat event in Salt Lake City.

title: Robotics and the future of on-orbit labor
summary: SpaceNews interviews Icarus Robotics CEO Ethan Barajas at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference about the role of robotics in future on-orbit labor. The discussion highlights advancements and challenges in space robotics.

title: Two astronauts replace ISS camera and docking aid on 6th-ever all-female spacewalk (video)
summary: NASA astronaut Jessica Meir and ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot replaced a camera and a docking aid during a 6-hour, 49-minute spacewalk outside the International Space Station on September 1. This was the sixth all-female spacewalk in history.

title: Scientists trace 7 stages of a meteorite's life, from hurtling space rock to Earth's surface
summary: Scientists have identified seven stages of a meteorite's journey from space to Earth's surface by studying 75 falling meteorites. This research provides new insights into the atmospheric entry and impact processes of space rocks.

title: Nonprofit wants to launch 80,000-year mission to Alpha Centauri in 2029 (video)
summary: A nonprofit organization plans to launch a small probe to Alpha Centauri in 2029 as part of the Fermi Explorer Mission, aiming to inspire further exploration and reflect on humanity's place in the universe.

title: On this day in space! Sept. 1, 1979: NASA's Pioneer 11 probe becomes 1st spacecraft to visit Saturn
summary: NASA's Pioneer 11 probe became the first spacecraft to fly by Saturn on Sept. 1, 1979. This historic mission provided valuable data about the planet and its rings.

title: NASA's Roman Space Telescope is just one of a few missions named after real-life women
summary: NASA's Roman Space Telescope, launched on Aug. 30, is one of the few missions named after real-life women. This highlights a trend of honoring female historical figures in space exploration.

title: 5 planets will light up the September sky — here's how to see them
summary: Five planets—Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn—will be visible in the September sky. Stargazers can observe them at specific times and locations.

title: Repairing the ISS 250 miles above Earth | Space photo of the day for Sept. 1, 2026
summary: ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot is seen outside the International Space Station (ISS) during a repair mission, highlighting the ISS's orbit 250 miles above Earth. The image underscores the challenges and scale of maintaining the orbital laboratory.

title: NASA Selects Blue Origin as Mars Telecommunications Network Provider
summary: NASA has selected Blue Origin to develop the Mars Telecommunications Network, a high-bandwidth communications system for Mars missions. The $700 million contract requires Blue Origin to deliver a telecommunications orbiter to NASA.

title: What’s Up: September 2026 Skywatching Tips from NASA
summary: NASA shares skywatching tips for September 2026, highlighting Venus, the Harvest Moon, and celestial events like the equinox. The guide includes spotting Antares, the Teapot constellation, and planetary alignments.

title: Historic Engines Take Their Place on Artemis III
summary: NASA technicians installed four RS-25 engines into the core stage of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket for the Artemis III mission, which is scheduled to launch in 2027. Each engine has a unique serial number tracking its flight history.

title: APOD: 2026 September 1 – A Plane Lunar Eclipse
summary: APOD features an image of a plane lunar eclipse scheduled for September 1, 2026. The event is highlighted as part of the Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) series.

title: Ice Island Survives Run-In With Joe Island
summary: In summer 2026, a large iceberg calved from Petermann Glacier in Greenland drifted into Nares Strait and collided with an island. The event was documented as the iceberg, named Ice Island, survived the impact with Joe Island.

title: NASA Welcomes Türkiye as Newest Artemis Accords Signatory
summary: NASA welcomed Türkiye as the 71st signatory of the Artemis Accords during a ceremony in Washington. The agreement promotes peaceful and transparent space exploration.

title: September 2026 Satellite Puzzler
summary: The August 2026 puzzler asks where a specific location is and what makes it unique. The context suggests it is related to a satellite image or space-related feature.

title: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Launches
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is scheduled to launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket on August 30, 2026. The telescope, named after NASA's first chief astronomer, will conduct wide-field surveys of stars and galaxies.

title: Roman Commissioning
summary: NASA's Roman Space Telescope is on a three-month journey to the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2 (L2) while undergoing commissioning to prepare for science operations. During this phase, systems are activated, adjusted, calibrated, and tested to ensure optimal performance.

title: APOD: 2026 August 31 – Launch of the Roman Space Telescope
summary: The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) announces the planned launch of the Roman Space Telescope on August 31, 2026. This mission aims to advance astronomical research and exploration.

title: Launch Site and Facility Progress ahead of East Coast Starship debut
summary: SpaceX is preparing for the upcoming Starship Flight 14 launch from Florida, with progress being made at the launch site and facilities. The event marks a significant step for SpaceX's East Coast Starship debut.

title: Launch Preview: Array of international launches planned this week
summary: Six international space missions are scheduled to launch from various global launch sites this week. The launches span multiple countries and organizations.

title: SLS picks up the pace, four vehicles in production
summary: NASA and its contractors are accelerating production of the Space Launch System (SLS), with four vehicles currently in development ahead of the Artemis III mission planned for next year. The progress marks a significant step toward the agency's lunar exploration goals.

title: NASA, SpaceX successfully launch the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Florida
summary: NASA and SpaceX successfully launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Florida. This marks a significant milestone in space observatory missions.

title: ESA awards first European Launcher Challenge contracts
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) has signed the first contracts under its European Launcher Challenge. This marks a significant step in fostering European launch capabilities.

title: Soyuz MS-28 departs the ISS, three spacewalks install upgrades to solar arrays and antennae
summary: The Soyuz MS-28 spacecraft departed from the International Space Station. Three spacewalks were conducted to install upgrades to solar arrays and antennae.

title: Starbase, Louisiana: The Largest Private Spaceport in the World
summary: SpaceX has announced plans to develop 'Starbase, Louisiana,' which will be the largest private spaceport in the world. The project aims to expand SpaceX's launch capabilities and infrastructure.

title: Starbase’s future production capacity ramping up
summary: Starbase's production capacity is increasing due to heightened activity at the facility. The expansion aims to support future space missions and Starship development.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon Heavy to launch Roman telescope, Falcon 9 to launch Starlink satellites
summary: Falcon Heavy is set to launch the Roman Space Telescope, while Falcon 9 will deploy Starlink satellites this week. Five orbital launches are planned from China, the United States, and French Guiana.

title: NASA’s Roman telescope nears launch, reaches final integration and rehearsal milestones
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is nearing its launch, scheduled for August 30, after reaching final integration and rehearsal milestones.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 key achievements. The publication marks five decades of the European Space Agency's contributions to space exploration and technology.

title: Phoenix 3: concept study for a reusable European spacecraft
summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and Earth return. The project aims to advance European spaceflight capabilities.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: Proba-3, a mission by the European Space Agency, will create an artificial solar eclipse to study the Sun's corona just before the total solar eclipse over Europe. The mission aims to provide unprecedented views of the solar atmosphere.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3 will experience a double eclipse as the Moon crosses its field of view. This event highlights the satellite's precision in observing solar phenomena.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona, which is otherwise difficult to study due to the rarity and brevity of natural eclipses.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to test their software aboard the Hera mission, a deep space asteroid mission. This provides a unique opportunity to run experiments millions of kilometers from Earth.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time during a drone flight at ESA's ESTEC technical center in the Netherlands. The payload was carried by a drone, marking a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will demonstrate formation flying with a coronagraph to study the Sun's corona while blocking out the Sun's disk. The mission involves two satellites playing a 'hide and seek' game to achieve precise alignment.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase innovative space startups and foster collaboration with Europe's space industry on September 16-17. The event aims to exchange ideas, discuss opportunities, and highlight capabilities at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands.

title: The Commercial-First Shift in National Security Space
summary: The space industry is shifting from a government-defined model to a commercial-first approach for national security space systems. This change involves leveraging commercial capabilities rather than solely relying on government-designed spacecraft.

title: Trump Orders Study To Establish US Space Academy
summary: Donald Trump has ordered a study to establish a US Space Academy, potentially adding a new service academy to the existing military academies. This move could introduce new competition in college football and other collegiate sports.

title: Exclusive: Helogen Plans Two In-Orbit Manufacturing Missions in October
summary: Helogen is planning two in-orbit manufacturing missions in October, marking the first flights of its HEL-IOS platform. The company has previously flown subsystems but this will be its first full platform deployment.

title: Fermi Explorer Wants to Reach Another Star for $15M
summary: The Starcloud cofounders announced the Fermi Explorer mission, aiming to launch humanity's first mission to Alpha Centauri by 2029 with a $15M budget.

title: Diffraqtion Adds to Pre-Seed Round for Quantum Camera Tech
summary: Diffraqtion secured additional funding for its quantum camera technology, bringing its total pre-seed investment to over $10M with contributions from Lockheed Martin Ventures and Sumitomo Corporation’s Presidio Ventures.

title: Roman Space Telescope Begins Its Journey to L2
summary: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from Kennedy Space Center, beginning its journey to Lagrange Point 2 for a commissioning period.

title: Launch Concerns Cast a Shadow Over SmallSat 2026
summary: The space industry faces significant launch concerns that could impact SmallSat 2026 if the current launch market conditions do not improve. Without changes, the industry risks hitting a major bottleneck.

title: ICEYE Opens Three International Offices in a Single Week
summary: ICEYE expanded its global presence by opening three international offices in a single week. This rapid expansion highlights the company's growth in the space industry.

title: Canadian Companies Partner on SDA Sat Solution
summary: Canadian companies are collaborating on a Space Development Agency (SDA) satellite solution. Meanwhile, SpaceX offers free SSA catalog access to smallsat operators, and LeoLabs prepares to demonstrate SDA for U.S. national-security missions under a $20.68M Space Force contract.

title: Space Weather Losses to Double by 2035, Report Finds
summary: A new report from Mission Space predicts that solar storms will cause $20.65 billion in losses by 2026, increasing to $44.27 billion by 2035. The rising economic impact highlights the growing threat of space weather to global infrastructure.

title: Inmarsat Maritime Launches New Safety Data Hub
summary: Inmarsat Maritime, now part of Viasat, has launched a new Safety Data Hub to provide insights and analysis of risks in global shipping. The product aims to enhance safety and operational efficiency for maritime stakeholders.

title: Kymeta Lands $20M DoD Order for Osprey u8 Satcom Terminals
summary: Kymeta secured a $20 million order from the U.S. Department of Defense for 100 Osprey u8 multi-orbit satcom terminals. The award includes multi-orbit connectivity capabilities.

title: Telesat Considers Space-to-Ground Optical Coms with Cailabs
summary: Telesat is exploring space-to-ground optical communications through a new collaboration with Cailabs. The agreement aims to integrate Cailabs' optical connectivity solutions for potential use in Telesat's operations.

title: Intuitive Machines Books 2-Satellite Order for Unnamed Customer
summary: Intuitive Machines has secured a two-satellite order for an unnamed commercial customer using its IM 300 platform. The platform has previously supported missions for the Space Development Agency.

title: Celebrating 40 Years of Via Satellite
summary: Via Satellite celebrates its 40th anniversary, marking four decades since its inception in 1986.

title: Via Satellite Editors and Writers Share Industry Memories
summary: Via Satellite celebrates its 40-year history of covering the space and satellite industry, sharing memories from its first edition in 1986 to the present.

title: Space Defense in 2040: A Networked, Weaponized, and Contested Frontier
summary: By 2040, space defense is expected to evolve into a networked and weaponized domain, leveraging autonomous systems, sensors, and AI for optimized targeting. The future of space warfare may prioritize rapid decision-making and action through orbital constellations.

title: Mapping the Future of Space in 2040:  From Constant Connectivity to AI-Powered Intelligence
summary: The article discusses predictions for the space industry in 2040, envisioning advancements like orbital data centers and AI-powered intelligence. It explores how these innovations could turn science fiction into reality.

title: Some Highs and Lows  of a 40-Year Journey in Space
summary: ViaSat celebrates its 40-year anniversary in 2026, reflecting on significant changes and opportunities in the space industry over the past four decades.

title: The ‘Impossible’ Shaping  a Better Future
summary: Via Satellite celebrates its 40th anniversary in 2025, highlighting a record 4,500 satellites launched globally, which is over twenty times the average annual cadence.
